facts.statement: The research was a retrospective cohort study covering patients who had fetoscopic myelomeningocele repair between 2014 and 2026.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The study included 209 patients, of whom 21 had a preoperative body mass index of 35 kg/m2 or higher.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Participants were divided into two groups based on whether their preoperative body mass index was 35 kg/m2 or higher, or lower than that threshold.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The proportion of babies born before 37 weeks of gestation was similar in the high body mass index group (52%) and the lower body mass index group (49%).
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The average gestational age at delivery was 35.9 weeks for the high body mass index group and 37.0 weeks for the lower body mass index group.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: After adjusting for other factors, a preoperative body mass index of 35 kg/m2 or higher was not associated with preterm birth.
facts.subject: humans
